CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain with right lower extremity tingling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bryan reports onset of lower back pain and right leg paresthesias ("pins and needles") yesterday afternoon following yard work (raking leaves). Symptoms began approximately 2 hours after coming inside his home. He had a similar episode approximately 3 years ago that resolved spontaneously within one day. He has tried conservative treatment with ice application and ibuprofen 200 mg (2 doses) without significant relief. Pain worsens with forward bending and improves with heat (hot shower) and sitting. He denies regular physical activity. He has not previously taken meloxicam.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for right lower extremity paresthesias. Pain exacerbated by forward bending, relieved by heat and sitting. Denies other neurological symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain episode 3 years ago that resolved spontaneously after 1 day

MEDICATIONS
None regularly. Recently tried ibuprofen 200 mg x 2 doses without relief.

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Denies regular physical activity or exercise. Lives with partner who was present at visit and corroborated severity of pain.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Not documented
General: Alert and oriented, appears uncomfortable
Back: Mild tenderness to palpation at L5 region. Pain with forward flexion. No pain with extension.
Neurological: Normal dorsiflexion bilaterally. Bilateral lower extremity pulses intact and equal. Right lower extremity paresthesias noted by patient.

RESULTS
Lumbar spine X-ray: Normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back sprain with right lower extremity radiculopathy secondary to acute muscular injury from yard work.

1. Rest and activity modification
2. Meloxicam prescribed for analgesia and anti-inflammatory effect
3. Physical therapy referral for stretching, strengthening, and conditioning given patient's sedentary lifestyle
4. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks
5. If symptoms persist or worsen, MRI will be obtained to evaluate for additional pathology
6. Patient agreed with treatment plan
